candidate_findings.title: Diagnostics freshness is nondeterministic
candidate_findings.claim: The timeout branch permits either last-known diagnostics or an empty set without defining the chooser, freshness marker, expiry, or consistent projection across editor, Problems, and Assistant context.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Users and agents can act on obsolete errors, or errors can disappear nondeterministically while different surfaces disagree.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define one version-keyed diagnostic freshness state machine for timeout, close, crash, restart, and replacement, including stale UI/AI provenance, expiry, and deterministic clear rules.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Timeout: show last known or empty; server crash → clear diagnostics, offer "Restart"
merge only in presentation surfaces such as Problems, editor markers, and Assistant/Interview context

candidate_findings.title: The no-server status rule conflicts with explicit degraded-state truth
candidate_findings.claim: The feature table says to omit status when no server exists, while later rules require visible overlap resolution, explicit degraded attachment, and fallback that cannot masquerade as healthy LSP.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Disabled, missing, misconfigured, installing, crash-looping, and partially attached states can become indistinguishable from healthy fallback or from each other.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Provide a state-to-surface matrix for no match, disabled, unavailable binary, installing, initializing, ready, partial, error, restarting, and fallback, including multi-server attribution.

evidence_refs.excerpt: No server: show nothing (omit)

candidate_findings.title: Executable server provisioning is not a closed security contract
candidate_findings.claim: The plan allows automatic downloads, auto-installs, custom commands, environment values, and initialization data, yet leaves the enablement default and executable trust mechanics unresolved.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A catalog, project, configuration, or compromised download path can cause arbitrary local or remote process execution or expose secrets through inherited environment state.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify per-server default posture, trusted-source allowlists, pinned versions and hashes/signatures, consent, install location and privileges, host placement, environment allowlisting/redaction, update/revocation/rollback, and offline/proxy failure behavior.

Optional auto-install (we can defer or limit; e.g. rust-analyzer from PATH, pyright/gopls optional install).

candidate_findings.title: External LSP content crosses into rendered UI and model context without a trust boundary
candidate_findings.claim: Server-returned Markdown and diagnostics are treated as dynamic external content and can enter Assistant/Interview context, but no sanitization, safe-link, prompt-injection, redaction, relevance, or size policy is stated.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A malicious project or compromised server can present unsafe links or markup, inject instructions into model context, leak source or diagnostic data, and consume unbounded context.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define Markdown/HTML and URI sanitization, command-link prohibition, provenance labeling, prompt-injection treatment, file and diagnostic selection, secret redaction, user consent, token/item caps, and truncation ordering.

candidate_findings.title: Server-originated CodeLens commands lack an execution policy
candidate_findings.claim: A CodeLens click may invoke a command such as running a test, while the stated FileSafe boundary covers rename, format, code actions, and workspace edits but does not cover CodeLens or general command execution.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An external server can potentially trigger processes or mutations outside preview, permission, cancellation, and audit controls.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define allowed command classes, server and capability provenance, confirmation and permission rules, workspace/host binding, mutation classification, FileSafe routing, cancellation, idempotency, and auditable outcomes.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Click invokes (e.g. run test)

candidate_findings.title: Supervisor lifecycle omits crash-loop and shutdown recovery semantics
candidate_findings.claim: Ownership, a happy-path protocol lifecycle, crash replay, and bounded backoff intent are named, but no complete transition table or deterministic retry, shutdown, and terminal-degradation behavior is supplied.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The implementation can create restart storms, orphan or duplicate processes, stale diagnostics, inconsistent session state, or replay unsaved documents in the wrong order.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify lifecycle states and legal transitions, retry count and backoff/jitter, crash-loop cutoff, initialization and shutdown timeouts, forced-kill and orphan cleanup, diagnostic clearing, replay order, cancellation, and user-triggered restart semantics.

evidence_refs.excerpt: the host owns local/remote placement and `/backoff/eviction`, the session owns lifecycle and restart behavior
Restart after `/crash` replays open documents
avoiding `/full-buffer-or-disk-resync`, uncontrolled auto-downloads, server-specific fragility, session/process duplication, weak status visibility, and unbounded `/backoff/eviction`

candidate_findings.title: Sync barriers and crash replay lack release and reconciliation semantics
candidate_findings.claim: Feature requests are gated behind sync barriers and crashes replay open documents, but the ordering of open/change/save/close, barrier completion, version reset, duplicate replay, send failure, and close/reopen races is not defined.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Requests may execute against an older server document, late results may update the wrong buffer version, or client and server text can diverge permanently after failure.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a per-session ordered synchronization queue, monotonic version and reconnect policy, barrier release condition and timeout, late-result suppression, replay idempotency, close/reopen handling, and a deterministic reconciliation path.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Client sends `textDocument/didOpen`, `textDocument/didChange`, `textDocument/didClose` (and optionally didSave).
feature requests are gated behind sync barriers so stale document versions do not leak into the UI
Restart after `/crash` replays open documents

candidate_findings.title: Mutation-capable LSP tooling is explicitly under-owned
candidate_findings.claim: The plan directly states that mixed LSP actions remain under-owned even though apply-edit paths span UI sessions, projects, workspaces, plugins, formatters, and internal-tool records.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Read-only intelligence and mutating operations can bypass one another's permission, routing, preview, or run-attribution boundaries and edit the wrong project or tab.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Assign a single authority and call graph separating reads from mutations; define session/project/host binding, permission and preview gates, FileSafe transaction semantics, denial and partial-failure behavior, rollback, and run-scoped audit records.

evidence_refs.excerpt: mixed `lsp` actions remain under-owned until UI-session reads and mutation_capable apply-edit paths are separated

candidate_findings.title: Per-root process fan-out has no resource envelope
candidate_findings.claim: Each monorepo package can become a root, each host/server/root tuple owns a process, and supplementary servers may coexist, but no process, memory, file-descriptor, queue, or diagnostic limits are defined.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Large monorepos or adversarial root layouts can spawn many heavyweight servers, exhaust local or remote resources, and block the UI or other projects.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Set global, per-host, per-project, and per-server session caps; idle TTL and eviction order; spawn concurrency and queue backpressure; diagnostic/request caps; prioritization; and visible degraded behavior when limits are reached.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Monorepo: each package.json is a root
supplementary servers may coexist only when their capability families are declared compatible

candidate_findings.title: Capability and position-encoding negotiation lacks a concrete oracle
candidate_findings.claim: The client promises to use only mutually advertised features and records version/position-encoding metadata, while forbidding over-advertisement, but supplies no exact client-capability matrix, version fallback, rejection behavior, or conformance fixtures.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Server differences can silently enable unsupported operations or mis-map positions, producing incorrect navigation, diagnostics, and destructive edits.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a versioned initialize-capabilities matrix, supported sync and encoding combinations, downgrade/reject rules, dynamic-registration behavior, server quirk policy, and deterministic transcript tests covering incompatible and malformed servers.

candidate_findings.title: SSH placement and path mapping have ownership but no trust contract
candidate_findings.claim: Remote server placement and path mapping are required, but the excerpt does not define host authentication, credential and environment forwarding, path-boundary validation, remote process privilege, or connection-loss recovery.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A wrong or compromised host can execute configured commands, receive secrets, map edits outside the selected worktree, or leave UI state falsely healthy after disconnect.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define trusted-host and known-host states, authentication authority, credential/env forwarding rules, canonical bidirectional URI mapping with traversal and symlink checks, remote spawn permissions, disconnect/reconnect transitions, cancellation, and user-visible host attribution.

candidate_findings.title: The trace service is named without data-handling or operations semantics
candidate_findings.claim: LspTraceService and tracing are selected, but no event schema, correlation model, payload redaction, retention, size cap, verbosity control, export policy, or operational alerts are stated.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Protocol traces can contain source text, file paths, diagnostics, initialization data, and environment-derived information, while unbounded logging can degrade performance or leak secrets.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define structured event names and IDs, mandatory metrics, redaction-by-default fields, payload sampling, retention and rotation caps, opt-in levels, secure export, crash-loop alerts, and tests proving secrets and source bodies are excluded.

candidate_findings.title: Configuration precedence and live reconfiguration are undefined

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The same project can spawn or stop different servers depending on load order, and the UI can show a setting that is not the effective source of truth.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define precedence among global, project, server, preset, environment, and explicit user values; provenance shown in Settings; schema validation; hot-reload versus restart behavior; invalid-value fallback; and migration/retirement of renamed keys and server IDs.
